findings.quote: | δ for T-1 (D2) | 0.05 | one new false conclusion in 20 decided ones |
findings.reason: The new_false denominator (decided atoms outside I, k = 0), counted on the power study's 50 development worlds: median 19 at α0, below 20 on 29 of 50 worlds; below 20 at 44% of the 8684 feasible k = 0 points of the 40 Q-40 draws; on 985 of 1684 defined world-draws (58%) the lower point of some T-1 pair has fewer than 20, so one wrong conclusion there exceeds δ. δ is below one-atom resolution on most worlds (protocol rule 9; v0.2's G8 failure mode). The denominator never falls along a pair (0 of 18 796).
findings.fix: Correct the δ rationale in §7; add granularity as a factor toward FAILS in §2; add a descriptive single-atom arm for T-1 (FAILS worlds in which every violating pair has at most one more wrong decided atom outside I at q than at p), printed next to the T-1 verdict.

findings.where: PREREG §4 T-1 HOLDS/FAILS sentences; §3.3; §7 power; audit/v03/aggregate.py
findings.reason: HOLDS asserts the claim without a quantifier, although up to 20% of worlds may violate it. FAILS reads as a refutation, although P(FAILS) is 0.50 at a per-world rate of 0.90 and 0.83 at 0.85 (§7). Protocol rule 16: an underpowered FAILS reads 'not demonstrated'.
findings.fix: HOLDS: 'T-1 holds on at least 80% of worlds (one-sided 95% Wilson bound): …'. FAILS: 'T-1 is not demonstrated: …; this does not show that the per-world rate is below 0.80'. Update the code and the wording tests.

findings.where: PREREG §4 (deterministic HOLDS sentence for G7a); §2 tautology bullet; audit/v03/aggregate.py:21
findings.quote: all_false because it contradicts every T-encoded atom, which the calibrated τ_d and τ_s exclude
findings.reason: The G7a HOLDS sentence omits that all_true scores (reproduced: the same 22 of 30 development worlds in every one of S2's 40 Q-40 draws, at α 0.95/0.90/0.85). echo, all_unknown and all_both score 0 by the definition of new_true (U or B on every H atom), so G7a tests only whether all_false is infeasible, which depends on the data (it needs a T atom in I and a small τ_d). The gate's minus world (N7) held on 7 of 100 development worlds, so a detector qualifier is likely; §6.2 does not anticipate it.
findings.fix: Add a fixed sentence printed with every G7a verdict giving the all_true count and levels, and stating that three of the four judged baselines score 0 by definition; correct the §2 'by construction' claim for all_false.
